newsitem.title: USA: Nextel sees progress despite 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Nextel sees progress despite 1996 loss.

text.p: Nextel Communications Inc on Friday said it was making solid progress in building an all-digital wireless network even though it posted a $556 million loss for 1996.
The company said it viewed its increased revenue, a record number of digital units in service and strong revenue per digital unit in service as positive indicators.
Nextel also said the launch of new national network capabilities and an aggressive national advertising campaign were helping it to achieve customer acceptance.
Revenues increased 94 percent in 1996 to $332.9 million, while 1,114,500 total wireless units were in service at the end of 1996, a 32 percent increase over the previous year's total.
Digital units in service increased 253 percent to 300,300 at December 31, while the monthly average revenue per digital unit increased 51 percent to $56 per unit.
Nextel said it was exceeding its operational and financial targets, more than tripling its number of digital subscribers.
Nextel's main investors include cellular phone pioneer Craig McCaw and Comcast Corp.
